why: B is the only one that survives the places the mark is actually seen. At 16 px and 20 px it is still a red bar through a line with ticks either side, while A loses its stem and head to a red smudge and C turns into a candle or pawn. A is the one the six rounds were stuck on: the tapered head reads as a funnel, wine glass or tee at every size above 20 px, and removing the neck did not change that. C fixes the funnel but adds a heavy square that outweighs the ruler and reads as a candlestick. B removes the object that kept being misread, and a playhead is a bar through a ruler in every editor, so the idea is carried by the geometry and not by a head. Its risk is that it reads as a text cursor or one red bar of a bar chart. The fixes below address that by making the ruler read as a ruler (equal gaps, mirrored major ticks, a heavier rule) rather than adding a head back.
polish_for_pick: Make the mark symmetric about the bar: set the left ticks at x 1.5, 3.5, 5.5 and the right ticks at x 10, 12, 14 (half-unit ticks, 1 unit gap to the 2-unit bar x 7 to 9 on both sides); today the left gap is 2.5 and the right gap is 2, which looks like an accident.
Put the taller 3-unit tick at the outer end of each side (x 1.5 and x 14) and keep the other four at 1.5 units, so the ruler reads as a ruler with end marks and not as a bar chart of uneven columns.

Thicken the rule to 1 unit (y 9.5 to 10.5, ticks standing on its top edge at 9.5) so the mark carries weight beside the 800 wordmark in the lockup; the ink to Rule-grey split stays exactly at the bar edges, x 7 and x 9.

Mirror the same layout in the 16 px drawing: ticks at x 1, 3, 5 and 10, 12, 14, a 4 px tick at x 1 and x 14 and 2 px ticks at x 3, 5, 10 and 12, bar x 7 to 9 and y 3 to 14 unchanged, so the favicon and the large mark are one design.
Keep the bar a flat Record rectangle (Rewind on dark) with no cap, notch or chamfer, and keep it 2 units wide (2 px in the 16 px drawing) so the favicon bar stays two full pixels.
